Deshaun Watson passed for 268 yards and moved the Browns into position for Andre Szmyt's career-long 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds remaining that gave Cleveland a 27-24 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday night. Watson, who completed 24 of 33 passes with a touchdown and an interception, was four of five for 46 yards as he led a go-ahead drive in the fourth quarter for the third straight week. The Browns - who are 3-1 for the first time since 2021 - had a 21-7 lead late in the first half before the Steelers rallied to tie it at 24-all. messages.text: Verstappen makes fast start in Malaysia to outpace Russell

metadata.summary: ​Max Verstappen made an impressively fast start to Formula 1's return to the Sepang International Circuit to set the pace from George Russell in the first practice session of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
metadata.content: Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Max Verstappen sets pace on F1's return to Sepang in first practice from George Russell | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Max Verstappen sets pace on F1's return to Sepang in first practice from George Russell Mercedes reveal major upgrade package in Practice One but Red Bull Max Verstappen sets the early pace at Sepang; Kimi Antonelli one second slower in fifth; watch second practice later on Friday at 9am with Qualifying on Saturday also at 9am, live on Sky Sports F1 Friday 2 October 2026 08:12, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Bernie Collins takes a look at Mercedes upgrades as they head into the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. ​Max Verstappen made an impressively fast start to Formula 1's return to the Sepang International Circuit to set the pace from George Russell in the first practice session of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. With F1 cars back on the popular track on the outskirts of Kuala Lumpur for the first time since 2017, Verstappen - the winner of that last race at Sepang - was quickly back in the groove in his Red Bull and set the pace on a 1:37.520 by three tenths of a second. Russell, who pipped Verstappen to victory in Baku last week, was second quickest in a Mercedes car that features a major aerodynamic upgrade this weekend. messages.text: Humphries dazzles on the doubles to reach Grand Prix quarter-finals

metadata.summary: Luke Humphries put in a much-improved display as his doubling prowess and a 10-dart finish secured a 3-0 rout of Jermaine Wattimena and a spot in the World Grand Prix quarter-finals.
metadata.content: World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries and James Wade storm into quarter-finals as Gary Anderson eliminated | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries and James Wade storm into quarter-finals as Gary Anderson eliminated Luke Humphries goes at 74 per cent on his starting doubles and 64 per cent on his closing ones as he sweeps Jermaine Wattimena 3-0, will face Niels Zonneveld in last eight after Dutch debutant dispatches Gary Anderson; James Wade excels against Stephen Bunting Friday 2 October 2026 00:23, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Humphries fired in a 10-dart finish as he swept Jermaine Wattimena aside at the World Grand Prix Luke Humphries put in a much-improved display as his doubling prowess and a 10-dart finish secured a 3-0 rout of Jermaine Wattimena and a spot in the World Grand Prix quarter-finals. There were also 3-1 victories for James Wade and Niels Zonneveld over Stephen Bunting and Gary Anderson respectively, while Gian Van Veen came through a deciding-set cracker with Ryan Searle to triumph 3-2. Humphries - the title favourite after defending champion Luke Littler's shock defeat to Luke Woodhouse on the opening night - had averaged only 80 and gone at 26 per cent on his closing doubles in a scruffy 2-0 win over Dave Chisnall on Tuesday evening. messages.text: 'I was terrified' - Sir Alex reveals all on Old Trafford return after brain haemorrhage

metadata.summary: Sir Alex Ferguson has said he was "terrified" about returning to Old Trafford following a brain haemorrhage.
metadata.content: Sir Alex Ferguson: Former Manchester United boss admits he was 'terrified' about making Old Trafford return after 2018 brain haemorrhage | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sir Alex Ferguson: Former Manchester United boss admits he was 'terrified' about making Old Trafford return after 2018 brain haemorrhage Sir Alex Ferguson underwent emergency surgery for a brain haemorrhage in 2018; Manchester United's most decorated manager returned to Old Trafford less than four months later after fearing he would lose his voice Friday 2 October 2026 08:00, UK Image: Sir Alex Ferguson admitted he was terrified about making Old Trafford return after his 2018 brain haemorrhage Sir Alex Ferguson has said he was "terrified" about returning to Old Trafford following a brain haemorrhage. Manchester United's most decorated manager underwent emergency surgery after falling ill in May 2018, and was placed in intensive care at Salford Royal Hospital. Speaking in 2021, Ferguson admitted that he feared losing his memory and his ability to speak, but has now revealed his emotions ahead of his return to the director's box at the Theatre of Dreams. The Scot was in attendance for United's 1-1 draw with Wolves, less than four months on from being admitted to hospital, and told BBC Breakfast that he was unsure what the response from fans would be towards him.
